query: How do you approach naming and branding a net-new security sub-category so it doesn't just read as a feature of the existing platform? Any examples where you built a brand for a new asset visibility or security concept from zero?

props.title: Making a New Security Sub-Category Stand on Its Own
props.subtitle: Naming and branding from zero
props.challengeSummary: You're asking how to name and brand a net-new security or asset visibility concept so it reads as its own category rather than a feature of an existing platform.

props.caption: The anthem video we made for Chorus's asset visibility brand

props.title: Give the Category Its Own Idea
props.content: Our approach is to build the sub-category around one idea it can own, then let the name and naming system follow from that idea. A name chosen from the parent platform's feature list will always read as a feature.

props.title: Chorus (Alphabet X): Creating an Eye-Opening Asset Visibility Brand
props.summary: We developed Chorus's brand narrative around "orchestration", wrote the brief for its visual identity system including a new logo, and later worked on product naming and nomenclature for its asset visibility platform.

final.explanation: Chorus is our closest example: an asset visibility platform from a startup within Alphabet's X, where the narrative came first and the product naming followed. It tracks goods rather than security, and we haven't published a case study on naming a security sub-category. For yours, we'd start by pinning down the one idea the category owns, before generating any names. Our Strategy Lead can scope that with you.
